name: TONGA

flag.title: Tonga
flag.note: Red field, white canton with red cross

lead: Tonga is the only Pacific island kingdom never ruled by a foreign power. It kept its royal family and its pride. Its 170 islands hide coral reefs, whale nurseries, and ancient stone arches.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Tonga's 170 islands stretch 800 km from north to south. In the west, volcanoes like Kao and Tofua rise from deep ocean. The eastern islands are flat coral limestone, barely above sea level.
The Tonga Trench plunges 10,800 metres nearby, one of Earth's deepest places. The Pacific plate slides under Tonga, so the islands nudge west each year. Earthquakes are common.
animals: Humpback whales swim to Tonga's warm waters every July to October to give birth and sing. You can snorkel beside them, which few places allow.
The flying fox, a fruit bat, is Tonga's largest native land mammal. It is sacred, and only the king may hunt it.
culture: Tongan society runs on strict rank. Chiefs stand above commoners. Every feast needs an umu, an underground oven heaped with pig, yam, and coconut cream.
Women weave fine pandanus mats that take years and are worth more than money at weddings. Tapa cloth, beaten from mulberry bark, is a royal gift.
history: The Tu'i Tonga dynasty began around 950 AD, one of the Pacific's oldest royal lines. At its peak it controlled trade across Fiji, Samoa, and Niue.

Captain Cook visited three times and called Tonga the 'Friendly Islands'. In 1875, King Tāufa'āhau Tupou I wrote a constitution before Britain could take control. Tonga joined the Commonwealth in 1970.
wows: Tonga is the only Pacific nation never formally colonised by a European power.
In Tonga, you can swim beside humpback whale mothers and newborn calves.
Tonga is often the first country to ring in the New Year.
The Ha'amonga 'a Maui, a 40-tonne coral arch from c.1200 AD, is Tonga's Stonehenge.
Commoners may not hunt Tonga's royal flying foxes.
Tonga's rugby team has beaten France and Italy at Rugby World Cups.
On average, Tongans are among the tallest and heaviest people on Earth.

myths.myth: Mother humpbacks sing to their calves
myths.fact: Only male humpbacks sing. Scientists think the songs help them find a mate.

myths.myth: Everyone in the Pacific speaks one language
myths.fact: The Pacific has over 1,000 languages. Papua New Guinea alone has more than 800.
